Tasks: 100 MTAC-IFBench instances. Configurations: 11 LLMs under Claude Code v2.1.14 (main); 8 LLMs under OpenCode v1.1.21 (harness comparison); constraint placement experiment on 30 sampled instances (policy file vs system prompt vs first-turn user prompt). Constant: harness, default API decoding parameters, same instructions and policy files. Baseline: none (models ranked against each other). Acceptance: per-item checklists verified by scripts and judge agents. Repetitions: not stated (single run). Human intervention: none during runs

GLM-5.2 best on instruction-following (CSR 80.4%, C-ISR 12.7%), Qwen3.5-27B lowest (CSR 60.6%); CSR 60.6-80.4% but C-ISR mostly below 10%, near zero after six turns for most models. Claude-Opus-4.6 best on functional correctness (FSR 90.2, F-ISR 37.0). C-ISR of all models well below F-ISR. Claude Code gives higher CSR/C-ISR than OpenCode (e.g. GLM-5.2 CSR 80.4 -> 76.8, C-ISR 12.7 -> 6.7), but OpenCode shows less decay over turns; rankings largely stable across harnesses (strong Kendall correlation, values not given in text). Policy-file constraints decay less than user-instruction constraints; updates harder than additions; policy-file placement gives the best compliance vs system or user prompt. No significance tests

Partly: benchmark separated models and harnesses and exposed decay over turns; automatic evaluation agreed with manual assessment (85.5-92.4%). Repeatability not assessed (single run, no variance reported). Limitations stated by the authors: possible judge biases (self-enhancement, verbosity), judge-agent cost, coverage of development scenarios

Limitations: potential evaluation bias of model-based judging; extra cost of judge agents; limited coverage of development scenarios (e.g. no security remediation or database migration). Gaps: existing benchmarks are outcome-oriented and single-turn; instruction-following in multi-turn agentic coding underexplored; agents weak on orchestration, project-wide consistency and quantitative control; harness should be standardised and reported; keeping important constraints in the repository policy file is advised
